title: P0 — fix the plugins' drift against today's bootstrap

Run it from a scratch folder inside the run's worktree (docs/scratchpad/k1-new/, which git ignores, so the repo's mise pins of yq apply) whose .config/bootstrap.toml holds [tools.git.branch.develop] merge_model = "pr" and [tools.git.branch.main] merge_model = "direct". Then run it from docs/scratchpad/k1-old/, whose file holds only the old [branch.develop] merge_model = "pr". Remove both folders after.
keeps.pass: The first folder prints pr for develop and direct for main. The second folder prints direct for develop (new key only, D4). A yq or mise error, or a non-zero return, is a fail.

decisions.decision: Where does P0 run?
decisions.ruling: One plan, in claude-plugins only. Every stale key, path, verb and flag is in this repo; bootstrap needs no change for P0.
decisions.rejected: A plan in each repo.

decisions.decision: The uncommitted DRAFT plan 2026-11-13-one-or-two-core-branches owns 9 of the files P0 edits. What happens to it?
decisions.ruling: Retire it into R3 (Recommended): Delete the draft folder now. Write a parked record so that R3 picks up its rulings (one or two core branches, no hard-coded develop). P0 then owns the files alone. The folder was moved out of the repo, and docs/memory/gaps/2026-11-14-one-or-two-core-branches-parked.md holds its rulings.
decisions.rejected: Keep it and revise it after P0; fold its work into P0.

decisions.decision: Do the drift checks of init, setup and doctor, which parse the old repo-sync dry-run output, belong to P0?
decisions.ruling: Include in P0 (Recommended): It is the same kind of drift: today the checks detect nothing. The fix is prose in 4 places (init SKILL.md, setup SKILL.md, doctor stack-checks.md). R3 replaces it later with `bootstrap check --json`.
decisions.rejected: Leave for R3.

decisions.decision: git-workflow reads the merge model with yq '.branch[B].merge_model'. Repos in the old [branch.<b>] form exist until a bootstrap sync migrates them. What does the new read do?
decisions.ruling: New key only: Read only `[tools.git.branch.<b>]`. A repo in the old form reads as `direct` until a bootstrap sync migrates it, which is today's silent behavior.
decisions.rejected: New key with the old key as a fallback.

decisions.decision: This repo's release docs (CLAUDE.md, the release skill, ci-and-releases.md) name [branch.main].merge_model, and so do the four p:*release tasks that the user edits by hand. What does P0 do with these docs?
decisions.ruling: Update docs; you edit tasks (Recommended): P0 changes the docs to `[tools.git.branch.main]`. The plan's index.md lists the four task files and `.config/bootstrap.toml` as a hand step for you, so the docs and the tasks match once you edit them.
decisions.rejected: Leave the docs unchanged.

decisions.decision: Is a review unit needed?
decisions.ruling: No. No unit lands runnable code: every owned file is prose, a template or a skill reference. The yq function in git-workflow is a snippet an agent runs from prose, and K1 proves it.
decisions.rejected: A security-review unit over wave 1.

decisions.decision: Execution mode.
decisions.ruling: teams (Recommended): wave 1 has four edit units, and U1 and U2 state the same key rule ([tools.git.branch.<b>].merge_model, absent reads as direct) in different files, so they can align the wording.
decisions.rejected: solo.

decisions.decision: What is the plan gate line?
decisions.ruling: mise x -- mise run code:precommit, with no --all. bootstrap's code-precommit task (repo/tools/pre-commit/tasks/code-precommit) and this repo's synced copy declare no flag and always run pre-commit with --all-files. This finishes B118 and closes the gap docs/memory/gaps/2026-11-06-gate-line-all-flag-undeclared-open.md.
decisions.rejected: Keep --all; ask bootstrap to declare the flag.

decisions.decision: bootstrap removed [overrides.gitignore] (migration M34). What does init's prose say instead?
decisions.ruling: Lines to add go into the repo's .gitignore directly; lines to remove from the shared .gitignore become [tools.git.files.".gitignore"] entries with "$mode" = "remove" in .config/bootstrap.toml.
decisions.rejected: None; this is a fact of bootstrap.

decisions.decision: The handoff reads docs/sync/tools/<tool>.md for each tool. Is that path valid?
decisions.ruling: Yes, with one exception: the claude tool's doc is docs/sync/tools/claude-tool.md. The handoff says so where it names the path.
decisions.rejected: None; this is a fact of bootstrap.

decisions.decision: Verification that the orchestrator keeps.
decisions.ruling: yq probe + stale grep (Recommended): K1 and K2 in gates.keeps. A real PR landing needs a forge, so it is not in the run.
decisions.rejected: Also a scratch-repo landing with a bare local remote.

decisions.decision: Landing consent.
decisions.ruling: Yes, merge and push: a fully green run merges to develop and pushes without a further prompt.
decisions.rejected: Ask before the merge.

decisions.decision: End an all run after P0 lands?
decisions.ruling: No, continue: the run continues with the old skills loaded until it ends.
decisions.rejected: End the run and ask for a restart.

decisions.decision: How do the drift checks read the new dry-run output of the bootstrap CLI?
decisions.ruling: By exit code and stderr. The CLI prints a last line, the headline: 'Dry run: no file would change' or 'Dry run: <n> file(s) would change', after a glyph or an [OK] tag. Exit 0 with 'Dry run: no file would change' and no 'bootstrap_commit would change to' line is no drift. Exit 0 with a headline of one or more files, or a 'bootstrap_commit would change to' line, is drift; the list lines (would change, would add, would seed, would remove) are the detail. Any other exit code is drift unknown, with the last stderr line as the reason; code 2 with 'run bootstrap init' means the values file is in an old form. Source: bootstrap docs/design/cli.md, section 'The output of a run', and cli/internal/repo/repo.go (the report writes to stderr).
decisions.rejected: Match any line that contains 'would change' (the no-drift headline contains it too).

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 1: the dry run exits 0 but prints no "Dry run:" headline (old repo-sync engine, or a stop before the file loop). What do init, setup and doctor report?
decisions.ruling: Drift unknown (Recommended): Drift unknown, with the reason "no Dry run headline: the repo's setup:configs runs an older sync engine; run bootstrap init". It is never green and never a guessed drift row.
decisions.rejected: Fall back to the old repo-sync rule when no headline is printed.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 2: D3 said "4 places" but names 3 parser passages. What does D3 mean?
decisions.ruling: 3 passages (Recommended): D3 means the three parser passages. doctor SKILL.md:290 stays unchanged, because the new list lines still begin with `would`. The plan records the correction.
decisions.rejected: Also reword doctor SKILL.md:290 to name the new words.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 3: docs-sync can flag a passage in a .claude/docs or .claude/skills file that U5 does not own. What does U5 do?
decisions.ruling: Own all .claude docs (Recommended): Widen U5's owns to `.claude/docs/**` and `.claude/skills/**`, which S1 already gives it. U5 can then fix any falsified passage there. No other unit edits those trees.
decisions.rejected: Report only, and leave the passage for a later plan.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 4: site vwf.md:3483-3484 says the plan gate needs --all because code:precommit alone checks only uncommitted files. What does U5 do?
decisions.ruling: Rewrite the reason (Recommended): U5 rewrites the sentence the same way U4 rewrites gates-consent.md and plan-doc.md: the plan gate runs the full hook pass over every file, because the task always runs pre-commit with --all-files and takes no flag. The same applies to any such sentence in ad-hoc-change.md.
decisions.rejected: Delete the sentence and keep only the gate line.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 5: U5 edits dprint-formatted files. How does it make them pass the code:format check?
decisions.ruling: dprint on owned files (Recommended): U5 may run `mise x -- dprint fmt <file>` on each file it changed, never on the whole tree and never `code:format --fix`. Then the unit gate must pass.
decisions.rejected: Re-pad and re-wrap by hand only.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 6: only `bootstrap init` migrates an old-form .config/bootstrap.toml (`sync` stops with code 2). When a unit names the remedy for an old-form repo in prose, what does it say?
decisions.ruling: Name bootstrap init (Recommended): Any prose that names the migration says "run bootstrap init", the words bootstrap itself prints. D4's ruling (new key only) does not change.
decisions.rejected: Name no remedy.

decisions.decision: Rulings review gap 7: the planners propose a gate line only when `mise tasks ls` lists it, but code:precommit is a hidden task. Fix the condition in P0?
decisions.ruling: Fix it in U4 (Recommended): U4 changes the condition to `mise tasks ls --hidden` in gates-consent.md and plan-doc.md, so hidden tasks such as code:precommit count.
decisions.rejected: Leave the condition out of scope.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 1: the repo root CONTRIBUTING.md:30 names [branch.<branch>].merge_model. No unit owns it. What happens?
decisions.ruling: U5 owns it (Recommended): Add CONTRIBUTING.md to U5's owns and to K2's scan. U5 changes it to `[tools.git.branch.<branch>]`, the same as CLAUDE.md (D5).
decisions.rejected: Leave it out of scope.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 2: git-workflow SKILL.md:156-158 and site vwf.md:3796-3797 say code:precommit checks only the working tree's changed files, but it always runs --all-files. What happens?
decisions.ruling: U1 and U5 rewrite (Recommended): U1 rewrites SKILL.md:156-158 and U5 rewrites vwf.md:3796-3797: code:precommit runs every hook over every file of the tree, with no flag. Nothing else in those passages changes.
decisions.rejected: Leave both passages out of scope.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 3: with BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1 the dry run prints verbose words, and D14 can miss a commit-only change. What do the checks do?
decisions.ruling: Unset it for the run (Recommended): The checks run `env -u BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE mise run setup:configs --dry-run`, so the output is always the non-verbose form that D14 reads. One parser stays.
decisions.rejected: Accept both forms of output.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 2, gap 4: on a non-zero exit, what text does the check use as the reason for drift unknown?
decisions.ruling: bootstrap's error + fix (Recommended): Report the exit code, the last bootstrap error line (it starts with `✗` or `[ERROR]`) and its fix line (`→ …`) when one follows, word for word. With no such line, report the last stderr line. The check does not guess the cause from the code; this replaces the "code 2 means old form" clause of D14.
decisions.rejected: Report the last stderr line only.

decisions.decision: Rulings review round 3, gaps 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 (one correct answer each, stated by the planner).
decisions.ruling: (1) K2 greps for the old yq expression with its leading quote, so the new line .tools.git.branch[ is no hit. (2) K1 runs in scratch folders inside the run worktree under docs/scratchpad/, where the repo pins yq; a yq or mise error is a fail. (3) p:plugins:local is not in the plan after_landing, because .config/vwf.yaml after_landing runs it after every green landing (change-plan gates-consent.md: do not propose a command already there). (6) The check matches the headline as the start of the last line after the glyph or [OK] tag, so count suffixes such as " · 161 unchanged" do not matter. (7) The init SKILL.md parser passage is lines 424-432.
decisions.rejected: (3) Record p:plugins:local as a plan after-landing step, which would run it twice.
